reference: Ernst, A. T., et al. "Staff scheduling and rostering: A review of applications, methods and models." European Journal of Operational Research (2004).
math_formula:
### Mathematical Model
A staff coverage assignment problem has sites R, employees E, shifts S, and skills K. Parameters are demand d[r,s,k], employee availability a[e,s], employee skill eligibility h[e,k], assignment preference cost c[e,k], and unfilled-position penalty w. Binary variable x[r,e,s,k] equals 1 when employee e is assigned to site r in shift s using skill k. Integer variable u[r,s,k] counts unfilled demand. Minimize sum_{r,s,k} w u[r,s,k] + sum_{r,e,s,k} c[e,k] x[r,e,s,k]. Coverage constraints require sum_e x[r,e,s,k] + u[r,s,k] = d[r,s,k]. Availability constraints require sum_{r,k} x[r,e,s,k] <= a[e,s]. Skill constraints require x[r,e,s,k] <= h[e,k]. Each employee can receive at most one total assignment: sum_{r,s,k} x[r,e,s,k] <= 1. Variables x are binary and u are nonnegative integers.
natural_language_example: A multi-site operations manager must assign available employees to shifts and skill roles. Only site-shift-skill combinations with positive required headcount need to be listed; all omitted combinations have zero demand. Employees can work only shifts where they are available and only roles for which they have the required skill. Assigning an employee to a role has a preference or mismatch cost, and leaving a required position unfilled has a high penalty. The goal is to minimize total assignment preference cost plus unfilled-position penalties while respecting availability, skill eligibility, and at-most-one-assignment-per-employee rules. This is not machine sequencing, job-shop scheduling, or flow-shop scheduling.
local_modification_notes: Internal OR-CPT version clarifies that this generator is compact staff coverage assignment with shortage slack and named site/employee/shift/skill indices, not generic machine sequencing. The internal staff sample used to shape demand is no longer exposed to LLM-facing prompts.
